name: Latin American, Caribbean, and Latinx Studies
notes: 40 credit hours (ten four-credit courses) of related coursework, of which 20 credit hours (five courses) must be core content courses - courses where at least 35% of the content engages with the region and its communities.

COURSE LISTS COME FROM THE DEPARTMENT'S MAJOR COURSE-LIST PDF (sas.rochester.edu/lacx/assets/pdf/lacx-major-courses.pdf), not from the major page itself, which only states the structure. The PDF is the authoritative list of courses that automatically count.

DIVISION IS DETERMINED BY YOUR COURSEWORK: 'To achieve a degree in the chosen division (humanities or social sciences), students must have completed at least 24 credit hours in the designated division, at least 12 of which (3 courses) must be a mid- or upper-level course in that division.' This entry is filed under humanities; if you take the social-science path your cluster requirement shifts accordingly. The planner does not count the divisional credit split.

REQUIREMENTS DELIBERATELY OVERLAP: 'Courses can be used to satisfy several knowledge requirements outlined in requirements I - VIII. This ensures flexibility given that not all courses are offered annually. However, a minimum of 40 credit hours must be taken to meet requirements.' The temporal-breadth, geographic-breadth and upper-level-writing groups below are therefore marked as reusable - they can be satisfied by courses already counted elsewhere.

INTERDISCIPLINARY SPREAD IS NOT ENFORCED: 'Students must take courses from at least three different departments or programs, and mid- and upper-level courses from at least two different departments.' Check that spread yourself.

GEOGRAPHIC BREADTH IS NOT FULLY ENFORCED: the rule is at least one course in TWO of the three geographies (Caribbean, mainland Latin America, U.S. Latinx diaspora). The group below asks for two courses from the combined list, so make sure yours fall in two different geographies.

LANGUAGE: students must demonstrate language proficiency; a maximum of twelve hours of language-learning courses (through the 200 level) can count toward the major. A student who places out takes no language course and needs another related course to reach 40 credits.
A maximum of four two-credit courses can count toward the major (the DANC options are 2-credit courses).

CAPSTONE: each student completes a capstone course or senior project approved by the LACX curriculum committee, and must present the capstone research at the annual major colloquium, the undergraduate research exposition, or an equivalent approved forum. Students wanting an alternate capstone work with the curriculum committee - these may include 391 independent study courses in the respective majors.

PETITIONS: students may petition for other courses to count when a significant portion of the research or community engagement relates to the major, including coursework in other disciplines, independent research, community-engaged courses, internships and study-abroad coursework. The major director and curriculum committee approve such petitions.

NEEDS VERIFICATION: the PDF lists 'ATHS 251 Inkas and their Ancestors' in the breadth tables but 'ATHS 221 Inkas and their Ancestors' in the introductory table; the catalog carries ATHS 221, which is what is used here. Sixteen other codes it names are absent from the 2025-26 catalog (among them CLTR 201, FREN 271, FREN 274, RELC 277, BLST 381, HIST 353/353W, and several SPAN courses), and the PDF gives some courses with and some without their W suffix - both forms are accepted where it does.

The PDF's geographic table is laid out in three columns that run across a page break; the column assignments below follow the extracted text and should be checked against the PDF itself for the entries near that break.

requirementGroups.label: Five mid- or upper-level courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Core Mid-, Upper-level Courses: Students must take at least five mid- or upper-level courses. Twelve credit hours (four courses) must be in the division of the degree. (Approved seminar capstone and upper-level writing courses are noted.)
requirementGroups.note: Twelve of these credit hours must be in the division you are taking the degree in - not checked by the planner.

requirementGroups.label: Capstone seminar
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Capstone (1): Each student will complete a capstone course or senior project that will be approved by the LACX curriculum committee. ... * Approved capstone seminar courses: AHST398; BLST381; HIST351W; HIST353W; HIST357W; HIST386W; HIST387W

requirementGroups.label: One further course from the LACX list (to reach 40 credits)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must complete 40 credit hours (ten 4-credit courses) of content related to the major, with 20 credit hours (five 4-credit courses) identified as core content courses. These are courses where at least 35% of the course content engages with the region and its communities.
requirementGroups.note: The named level requirements account for nine courses; at least one further approved course is needed to reach the 40-credit minimum, and more if you place out of the language requirement or use 2-credit courses.

requirementGroups.label: Temporal breadth: pre-colonial or colonial
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Time period requirement (2): Students must take at least one pre-colonial or colonial course and one modern course. These courses may also count toward the core content requirement.

requirementGroups.label: Temporal breadth: modern
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Time period requirement (2): Students must take at least one pre-colonial or colonial course and one modern course.

requirementGroups.label: Geographic breadth: two of the three regions
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Geographic requirement (2): Students must take at least one course in two of the following three geographies: Caribbean, continental Latin America, and U.S. Latinx diaspora.
requirementGroups.note: Your two courses must be in two DIFFERENT geographies - see the program notes. Caribbean: CLTR260, BLST216, BLST237, BLST381, FREN274, HIST150, HIST151, HIST158, HIST248W, HIST251W, HIST255/SPAN255, HIST386W, SPAN235, SPAN251, SPAN273. Latinx diaspora: AHST247, ANTH239, ANTH252, HIST149, HIST158, HIST252W, CLTR201, RELC234, RELC284, SPAN159, SPAN206, WRTG266. Mainland Latin America: the remaining entries in the list.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses from the LACX list
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Students must complete two upper-level writing courses, in accordance with University requirements. ... † Course satisfies upper-level writing requirement.
upperLevelWriting.note: Where the PDF names both a base course and its W section (HIST 248/248W, HIST 251/251W, HIST 252/252W), register for the W section.
